question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India deal with the right to equality?
solution:
The correct answer is __**14 to 18**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Article 14 to Article 18 of the Constitution of India guarantees the right to equality for every citizen of India. 
 
• This deals with the general principles of equality.
 
• Article 14 of the constitution states that:
 
 
• The State shall not deny to any person equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws within the territory of India.
 
• This article constitutes of 2 parts, being:
 
 
• Equality before law and
 
• Equal protection of the laws
 
 
 
 
 
• Article 15 prohibits discrimination against citizens on such specific grounds as religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth.
 
• Article 16 guarantees equality of opportunity in matters of employment under the state. The right is available to citizens only.
 
• Article 17 deals with a peculiar problem in our country. Howsoever praiseworthy the caste system in its origin might have been, it certainly proved to be a disgrace to humanity, a threat to unity, and a serious hindrance to the social, educational, and economic progress of our country. 
 
• Article 18 abolishes titles, other than a military or academic distinction.
